$schema-note: One theme preset (design brief 2026-08-27, §4.6). A preset is a complete designed look: two authored palettes, a type map for all four roles, shape and texture and density, a motif default, and the curated option sets from the visual story.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings — the generator writes the RGB triples (brief §3.6). The dark palette is authored value by value; no dark value is derived from its light twin.
$safety-note: Lines are told apart by their letter and their name first. A line colour, where a client sets one, is a second signal and never the only one (brief §8.1).
label: Atlas
summary: A mapped city on its transit network. A survey sheet and a departure board at once: lines, stations, transfers.
$palette-words-light: surveyor's paper, india ink, route red, contour grey, graticule pale blue, key-box white, platform slate, benchmark silver
$palette-words-dark: deep slate ground, cool white ink, lit route marker, sunken contour grey, felt-grid blue, map-case grey, signal-white label, night platform blue
$font-note: Brief §9.3. Atlas points both value roles at Overpass Mono on purpose: a timetable and a coordinate are the same kind of value.
$tokens-note: Preset-level remaps of existing tier 2 and tier 3 tokens. No new property name (brief §3.4). The map grid is held below hairline contrast and never becomes an image. --schedule-trace-width is the traced line (visual story, moment 3): the departure board's forward column connects down the sheet. It is zero in every other preset, and a zero-width bar paints nothing at all.

headingFace.label: Heading face
headingFace.prompt: The sign face. Body stays Libre Franklin and data stays Overpass Mono under every option. Every option must hold at nameplate size, at the h3 step, and inside a route mark.

choices.label: Overpass
choices.why: The highway sign. It is drawn from road lettering, so route marks, station names, and transfer lines all speak in the voice the story needs.

choices.label: Libre Franklin extrabold
choices.why: Franklin Gothic set American transit and news signage for a century, so running the body face up to heading size keeps the system whole and costs nothing extra.

choices.label: Archivo Condensed
choices.why: Sheet space is scarce on a real map, and condensed headings pull the page toward the drawn sheet, which suits a dense multi-venue programme.

choices.label: Corner title block
choices.why: Hairline frame, coordinate marks at two corners, city and date range below, schematic line-diagram divider under it. The corner of a survey sheet that carries a network.

choices.label: Sheet header with a scale line
choices.why: A scale bar states an extent, which is what a date span is, so the device stays honest.

choices.label: Departure board header
choices.why: The concourse board rather than the sheet, for events whose story is movement more than geography. The line updates on load and on user action only.

choices.label: Departure board
choices.why: Time down, lettered lines across, faint map grid behind, traced-line signature interaction. The theme's clearest idea.

choices.label: Line diagram
choices.why: The strip map inside a carriage: one line at a time as a Beck-style vertical run, which serves a visitor following one track all day.

choices.label: Gazetteer list
choices.why: A gazetteer indexes a map by place, which serves a visitor choosing where to stand rather than where to go.
